messages:
deploy-bot: deploy started: release/2026-03-18 (canary -> dedicated-canary) :rocket:
sanjay: seeing p95 jump on dedicated canary right after that deploy, routing looks noisy. customers report tail latency up ~2x :grimacing:
lucy: which workload? heavy-seq or mixed?
sanjay: mixed but skewed to medium sequences. profiler shows hot loop in kernel selector: lots of oscillation between AVX-optimized kernel and generic fallback, causing extra memcopies. attaching snippet:
```
# flame: /tmp/flame-228123.svg
hot function: kernel_selector::choose
self  48.2%   48.2%  kernel_selector::choose
self  21.1%   69.3%  kv_cache::ensure_prefetch
self   8.9%   78.2%  autobatch::slice
```
eva: interesting — logs show kernel hint from scheduler frequently toggling for same model and seq len. suspect change in merge 9a7b3c1 (autobatch heuristics) that updated hint TTL and batching thresholds.
sanjay: I ran a quick bisect locally, narrowed perf regression to PR #4128 which changed `autobatch::hint_expiry` -> 50ms to 1ms and added LRU hint eviction.
kevin: that PR also touched kernel routing weights (k_routing) in kernel-selector. probably made selector too eager to pick cheaper kernel that doesn't handle KV cache efficiently. can we revert the two lines?
lucy: putting dedicated canary rollout on hold. SLA risk for two paying Dedicated customers flagged by account team. @kevin can you open an emergency revert? :exclamation:
kevin: opening revert PR now: revert/4128-autobatch-hint-ttl. will queue rollback to canary once CI passes. CI perf tests show 18% p95 reduction when I flip back the TTL locally.
eva: also add a quick test to CI that runs a 1-min mixed seq perf profile and asserts p95 delta < 10% vs baseline. this would have caught it.
sanjay: ack. I'll escalate to oncall if rollback doesn't land in 15m. adding note to the dedicated rollout thread and pinging customer success. :phone:
